evidence.section: 3.2 Tensile properties at various testing temperatures
evidence.quote: the current titanium alloys present superior engineering tensile strength of 519 MPa at 700 °C.

evidence.section: 3.2 Tensile properties at various testing temperatures
evidence.quote: The ultimate strength of the (TiBw + (TiZr)5 Si3 )/Ti55 composites at 700 °C (519 MPa) was similar to that of the Ti55 alloys at 650 °C (509 MPa)
in the temperature range of 650–700 °C, the decline extent of the dislocation strengthening /Delta1σdis ( ∼109 MPa) was equivalent to the reduction of the peak-stress /Delta1σpeak ( ∼98 MPa)
in the temperature range of 70 0–80 0 °C, the /Delta1σpeak ( ∼226 MPa) was much higher than the /Delta1σdis ( ∼174 MPa)

For titanium and its alloys, it is generally believed that a significant DRV occurred when deformed above 550 °C [33] . Thus, the increase of slope above the critical temperature could be attributed to the enhancement of DRV.
the temperature range of 25–800 °C can be subdivided into three stages: ( Ⅰ ) the hardly DRV stage below 600 °C, ( Ⅱ ) the obvious DRV stage above 600 °C, and ( Ⅲ ) the DRX stage above 700 °C.
the strengthening effect of multi-scale architectures is underpinned as the enhanced dislocation strengthening owing to the introduction of thermally-stable heterointerfaces
the contribution of the effect of dislocation density on the peak stress can be described as Eq. (16)
the high-temperature softening was dominated by the DRV when the temperature was below 700 °C
the CDRX assisted by the micro-deformation bands was gradually transformed into discontinuously dynamic recrystallization (DDRX)
Such characteristics of recrystallization were often suggested to be the CDRX
PBS was another softening mechanism at 700 °C
